text.title: The Curator's Hands
text.declared_genre: Alternative Hip-Hop / Acoustic Folk / Spoken Word
text.declared_mood: Wry, reflective, uneasy, self-interrogating → tender, accountable, quietly resolved
text.production_notes: Fingerpicked acoustic guitar with subtle percussive taps, Lo-fi drums, brushed snare, soft kick, warm bass, Sparse piano and muted strings enter halfway, Gentle room noise, chair creaks, breath kept in, Occasional dropouts before key lines, Arrangement feels like a late-night gallery tour becoming a confession,
text.vocal_notes: Intimate male vocal, Spoken-word rap with conversational timing, dry humor, and careful pauses, Soft sung refrains, slightly fragile but warm, Starts detached and museum-guide ironic, then grows more personal, Close-mic delivery, occasional whispered doubles on key phrases, Final section more melodic and human,
section_names: Final Refrain – sung, fuller but restrained

transcription.text: Welcome back. Please keep your hands away from the glass, and on this, of course, they're mine, in which case, that explains most of the fingerprints. I used to call myself curator like that made it clean, like arranging the wreckage was different from making the scene, a thousand little fragments all polished in frame, tiny borrowed torches, all speaking one name, I'd stand in the middle with the clickboard and grin like none of this is chaos if I organize it thin. Here's the long wing, here's the father display, here's the childhood exhibit, please don't lean that way, here's a small angry room where the comments still live, here's the joke I keep telling so I don't have to forgive, and here behind glass is the part I call art, a nervous little animal pretending to be smart. Oh, curator, what did you keep? What did you bury to make the room look deep? Oh, curator, who did you become? When every thousand voices had to answer as one? See, the label said mixed media, personal history, which is a polite way of saying please don't ask directly, the label said leave period self-arrangement, which is a polite way of saying I was scared of the basement, the label said the themes of distance, class and restraint, which is a polite way of saying I wanted help and couldn't complain. And people nodded because labels are magic when they're printed small, you can hide a whole collapse on a white museum wall, you can call it material tension, when the material is grief, you can call it negative space, when what's missing is belief, you can call it found object when the object is a child, left into many rooms and told to be mild. Oh, curator, what did you move? What did you soften so the story felt smooth? Oh, curator, tell me the truth, did you protect the peace or protect yourself from proof? I found the old notes, not dramatic, just a folder with dates that looked harmless, little records of attempts to make the shape behave too bitter, too ornate too direct too much, not enough. Try again but make it sound like someone survived it, that one hurt, because I did sort of, depending how generously you define survived, I kept trying to make a person out of evidence, but every time I trim the edges, I lost the fingerprints, every time I made a balance, it stopped breathing right, every time I made it pretty, I forgot the night, there's a difference between care and control, I learned that light, which is on brand, maybe I wasn't making meaning, maybe I was making distance, maybe I kept the hard parts beautiful, oh, nobody would touch them, maybe I called it a gallery, because storage unit for pain is terrible branding, maybe the earlier version of me wasn't wrong, just lonely with better lighting, so here's what I know now, the hands matter, not because they made everything for nothing, nobody does, we inherit rooms, we borrow phrases, we must remember whether we keep what cuts us, because at least it proves something made contact, the hands matter, because they choose, this shard not that run, this silence, not yet, this wound with the chair beside it, this joke, so the wound doesn't think it owns the house, the hands matter, because they return, because they keep for you ranging, what they couldn't repair, because they look the same piece again and again and whisper, maybe not beautiful, but honest there, oh creator, open the room, leave some dust and leave some gloom, oh creator, let it be touched, not everything fragile has to mean to my joke, creator, lower the light, let the crooked things stay, crooked tonight, if a thousand voices still answer as one, maybe the name they speak isn't finished, just begun, so yes, the fingerprints in mind, the cracked frame too, the missing label, the overlong explanation, the unnecessary matter for me, if the act is it, I'm not proud of the room, but I know why each one's there, and for once I'm leaving the doors unlocked,
